verdict.root_cause: cartservice requests are slow but successful, and all the added latency sits inside cartservice's own Redis client spans: every HGET and HMSET consumes a tightly clustered ~300-310ms while the enclosing gRPC handlers use under ~2ms of self-time, and operation latency scales exactly with the number of Redis round trips (GetCart ~305ms with one command, AddItem ~600-615ms with two) [tr_90b319a4de65]. A fixed, non-long-tailed per-round-trip penalty with no errors, refusals or retry inflation is the signature of an artificial egress delay on the cart-to-Redis path rather than a loaded Redis server. The change record supplies exactly that mechanism: six identical automated cycles attaching a traffic-shaping container with a fixed egress delay to the cart-service network namespace, all by platform-automation and shaped like scheduled fault injection [tr_b2edbcc002b7]. The record claims each attachment was removed and shows nothing within ~78 minutes of onset, but the traces at 17:17 are incompatible with a clean namespace, so the likely reading is a further unlogged cycle or a removal that was recorded while the qdisc/sidecar persisted. frontend and checkoutservice alerted seconds later because they sit above cartservice and inherit the wait, with their own error ratios at or below baseline [tr_c69149eb2037][tr_6dc7761805cb].
verdict.reasoning: Traces localise the fault to cartservice's Redis client spans with ~1ms of cartservice compute, exactly the expected command count, no error-status spans, and a narrow 300-310ms band across all ten traces — ruling out cartservice code, retry storms, other checkout dependencies, and outlier-only tails [tr_90b319a4de65]. The failure is a wait, so the class is dependency_latency; an injected delay in the call path is classified by the wait it causes, not by the edit that inserted it. cartservice is named because the delay is on its egress and both upstream callers' symptoms follow from it [tr_90b319a4de65][tr_c69149eb2037]. Supporting negatives: cartservice logs continuous normal cart operations to the window edge with no panic, restart, or connection-refused text [tr_752c2f0ccdd5], and checkoutservice completes full order flows at info severity in the final minute [tr_6dc7761805cb]. The change record is evidence for the mechanism, not the verdict; I decline its own bookkeeping claim that no injection was active at onset, because the traces measure the delay directly. Fix is removing the injected shaping on the cart-service namespace, not an image rollback.
open_questions: Whether an unrecorded seventh injection cycle began near 17:15:45, or a logged removal left the tc/netem qdisc or sidecar in place — nothing inspected the cart-service namespace during the incident.
redis-cart was never queried: no server-side latency, connection, or slowlog evidence, so Redis-side slowness is only inferred against from the delay's uniformity.
cartservice has no usable metric series in either window, leaving its latency percentiles, request rate, restarts, and readiness unmeasured [tr_b574bd4252ae].

alternatives.root_cause: redis-cart itself became slow (server-side saturation or blocking persistence), adding ~300ms to every command.
alternatives.why_not: A genuinely loaded or blocking Redis produces variable, long-tailed latency; the observed penalty is uniform at 300-310ms across command types and all sampled traces, and no Redis-side signal was gathered to support it [tr_90b319a4de65].

alternatives.root_cause: A REDIS_ADDR override left cartservice pointed at an alternate Redis port, so cart traffic traverses a slower or proxied endpoint.
alternatives.why_not: Each REDIS_ADDR override has a logged revert, the last ~1.3h before onset, and a wrong endpoint would more typically yield refusals or a step change rather than a precise fixed per-round-trip delay [tr_b2edbcc002b7][tr_90b319a4de65].

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating the container gives cartservice a fresh network namespace, dropping any residual tc/netem qdisc or attached shaping sidecar left by the injection cycles. In Tempo, new cartservice HGET/HMSET spans should fall from the ~300-310ms band to single-digit ms, GetCart from ~305ms and AddItem from ~600-615ms to a few ms, and frontend GET roots from ~306-312ms to low tens of ms.
proposal.if_wrong: If post-recreate traces still show ~300ms Redis spans, the delay is not in cartservice's namespace - look at redis-cart (never queried) or host/bridge-level shaping. If latency drops then returns on a ~10-20 min cadence, a live injection schedule is still running. cartservice has no usable metric series, so confirmation rests on trace durations only.
proposal.risk: Chosen over config_revert because change history shows no net config delta and the final REDIS_ADDR revert was ~1.3h pre-onset, so there is no bad config to restore. If the delay is actually server-side or host-level, this changes nothing and burns time on an unrecoverable action: the recreate discards cartservice's in-process cart cache and is not reversible. It also destroys the namespace evidence needed to confirm the qdisc hypothesis - inspecting the namespace first would be strictly better.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice for the seconds it takes to recreate; frontend (AddItem, GetCart) and checkoutservice (GetCart, EmptyCart) see connection resets and may surface brief user-facing cart errors, which would appear as a short error-ratio blip on both.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Four services alerted within 30 seconds spanning cart, frontend, and checkout paths, which is more than a single isolated warning and cannot be dismissed. The cartservice-first ordering with downstream fanout hints at a shared dependency or backing store, but no evidence exists yet.
